dedupe_keys.name: nlr evi dist distribution feeder and service transformer impacts of ev charging with smart charge management

description: EVI-DiST (Electric Vehicle Infrastructure - Distribution System Integration Tool) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) tool for high-fidelity modelling, analysis and control of EV charging on distribution grids. Contents: it assesses how growing EV adoption affects distribution systems from the feeder level down to detailed secondary models of homes and businesses, including service transformer loading, winding hot-spot temperature and degradation, primary feeder component capacity and service voltage profiles, and compares fixed controls such as time-of-use charging with adaptive algorithms using real-time grid conditions; a web dashboard shows results. It integrates with EVI-Pro, DiTTo, HELICS, OpenDSS, ResStock, ComStock, CYME and Synergy. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research, part of EVI-X. Coverage: US utility feeders; the page says it has informed grid planning with major utilities in more than five states, with a 2025 report on Colorado feeders. Format and access: open source code on GitHub linked from the NLR page. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): BSD-3-Clause. Simulation uses: hosting capacity and transformer upgrade planning for EV loads, and testing managed charging strategies in co-simulation. Related records: platform-opendss, platform-helics, model-resstock and model-comstock. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
